_purpose: Versioned 'expected structure' manifest for a rendered enablement-html-renderer artifact. Each entry names one structural feature the CURRENT canonical template (renderer-template.html) provides, plus a detection rule a checker can run against an already-rendered .html file to see whether that feature is present. Feeds KTLO B-01's drift checker (T-B01-02, a separate task in ai-os-personal-ktlo--2026-07-28) - never edited by that checker, only read by it. Update this file whenever renderer-template.html gains, changes, or removes a structural feature; it versions alongside the template, not the other way round.

defined_at.known_version_field_drift: FIXED in the same change that added this contract (plugin bumped 1.3.2 -> 1.5.4; see CHANGELOG.md [1.5.4]). While grounding this manifest's `introduced_in` fields, discovered that VERSION had been regressed from 1.5.1 down to 1.3.1 in PR #41 (2026-07-21, commit 217a708) - a merge from a branch that had diverged before the 1.4.0/1.5.0/1.5.1 work landed, which silently deleted those three releases' CHANGELOG entries too - then continued forward from the wrong number to 1.3.2 in PR #45 (2026-07-27, commit ebbc0f5). Restored the three lost CHANGELOG entries verbatim and renumbered the two mislabeled ones (1.3.1 -> 1.5.2, 1.3.2 -> 1.5.3) so the record is chronologically honest again. Each feature's `introduced_in` below still cites PR number and commit SHA rather than the semver at time of authorship, since that remains the more precise anchor regardless of version-field health going forward.

features.label: Theme-aware diagrams (normalizeSvg remaps legacy hardcoded hex to currentColor/var(--accent)/var(--accent2)) PLUS a manual light/dark toggle button - theme must not depend on prefers-color-scheme alone (the B-25 fix in ai-os-jc-toast KTLO)

introduced_in.note: 'v1.4.0 - manual light/dark toggle' (VERSION read 1.4.0 at this commit). normalizeSvg's legacy-hex remap already existed at the #21 import.

features.label: Auto-linking of bare http(s) URLs at render time across plain-text fields (linkifyPlain) and inside trusted prose HTML, text nodes only (linkifyProse)

features.label: Theme-variable accent palette: --accent / --accent2 custom properties defined for both light and dark, with SVG text/stroke inheriting ink via currentColor (so diagrams flip with theme)

features.label: Print output is always light mode, regardless of the reader's manual dark-mode toggle or OS preference - :root's theme variables are reset with !important inside @media print, and the comic panel background is forced back to cream, so diagrams and callouts never render dark-on-white on paper or in a PDF export

introduced_in.commit: n/a (pending merge at contract authoring time)
introduced_in.note: Fixes a real bug: :root[data-theme="dark"] has higher CSS specificity than the plain :root the pre-existing @media print block edited, so a reader who had manually toggled dark mode got dark-on-white diagrams and callout boxes when printing or exporting to PDF. The OS-only prefers-color-scheme path had the same gap. !important on the print :root block is required, not just later source order, because it must beat the higher-specificity :root[data-theme] rules regardless of which theme state the reader is in when they print. This is the SOT copy of the fix; ai-os-personal ported it separately since the two templates have diverged in spacing/Jira-linking since v1.5.1.

not_covered_by_this_contract: Comic character linework (#1a1a1a on the fixed cream comic panel) is intentionally NOT flagged by accent-palette-v1 or any other check here - it is a deliberate fixed-appearance design choice (CHANGELOG 1.1.0), not a dark-mode legibility bug. A future 'no unexplained hardcoded hex' check would need an explicit allowlist for the FACE/EYES/BROW/ACCENT maps and the .cmds/.callout.warn chrome to avoid false positives; out of scope for v1.

print-light-forced-v1 checks the source markup for the fix's presence, not that a real browser actually resolves the cascade correctly. The renderer-template.html README/CHANGELOG for this fix name the manual print-and-verify step as the real acceptance test; this regex check is a regression net for the source, not a substitute for opening a printed PDF.
